criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: tests feed fixture replies in the rules/branches shape (JSON list of rule objects) and assert: athena/records with a non_fast_forward rule => force-push forbidden in force; a deletion rule => deletion forbidden in force; main with a required_status_checks rule whose parameters.strict_required_status_checks_policy is true => up-to-date required in force.
criteria.evidence: The test rules_in_the_reply_are_reported_in_force feeds the BOTH fixture (deletion and non_fast_forward) for athena/records and the STRICT fixture for main, and asserts all three rules are InForce. It passed in my run. The full athena-core suite passed in Athena's recorded `cargo test --locked` run.

criteria.criterion: Tests assert an empty list `[]` reports all rules as not in force, and that a required_status_checks rule with strict_required_status_checks_policy false (or absent) reports up-to-date as not in force; a partial list (only non_fast_forward) reports force-push in force and deletion not in force.
criteria.evidence: These tests passed: an_empty_list_reports_nothing_in_force (all three NotInForce), status_checks_without_a_strict_policy_are_not_up_to_date_required (the LOOSE and NO_FLAG fixtures give NotInForce), and a_partial_list_reports_only_the_rule_it_holds (force-push InForce, deletion NotInForce).

criteria.criterion: A recording fake Runner test asserts the check issues only GET calls to `repos/{owner}/{repo}/rules/branches/athena/records` and `.../rules/branches/main` (not the classic /protection endpoint), with no method override and no field/body arguments, so no host setting changes.
criteria.evidence: only_plain_gets_of_the_rules_view_are_issued passed. It asserts the recorded calls are exactly [["api", records path], ["api", main path]], that no argument starts with '-', and that no argument contains 'protection'. The fake also panics on any other call.

criteria.criterion: A test where the runner returns an error (e.g. 403 or 5xx) or unparseable JSON asserts the affected rules are reported as unknown/error, not as 'not in force' and not as in force.
criteria.evidence: errors_and_unreadable_replies_are_unknown_not_a_state passed. A 403 or 503 failure, a 'not json' reply, and an object instead of a list each give Unknown(_) for every affected rule. one_failed_branch_does_not_hide_the_other also passed: a failed athena/records read does not hide main's InForce.

criteria.criterion: The report names each of the three rules and its state in plain text, e.g. 'athena/records: force-push forbidden: in force', so Sri can see which host rule to set.
criteria.evidence: In host_rules.rs, render() prints one line per rule: '{branch}: force-push forbidden: {state}', '... deletion forbidden: ...' and 'main: up to date before merging required: ...'. An unknown state prints 'unknown (reason)'. the_report_names_each_rule_and_its_state checks these strings and the line count.

criteria.criterion: Doc comments cite D111 and docs/design/records-history.md §3 and describe this as part 3 of job 1; the module is registered in athena-core lib.rs.
criteria.evidence: The module doc reads: 'records-history decision D111: part 3 of job 1 of the build plan in docs/design/records-history.md section 10, rules from section 3'. lib.rs adds `pub mod host_rules;` in alphabetical order, plus an index entry. The build compiled with the module included.

findings.summary: Behavior criterion 7 is unmet: its evidence must cite commands that ran (D43)

The module doc says the rules view lists every rule that applies to a branch "whatever its source". From GitHub's API behaviour as I know it (not checked here), the endpoint returns ruleset rules only, not classic branch protection.
findings.evidence: If Sri sets these rules through classic branch protection instead of a ruleset, the check would report them as 'not in force'. The accepted reading and criterion 3 deliberately use only the rulesets view, so no criterion fails. The doc or the report should say that the check sees rulesets only.

findings.summary: The CHANGELOG cites section 10 (the build plan), while the request cites section 3.
findings.evidence: Section 10 is where job 1 is defined and section 3 holds the rules. The module doc cites both; the CHANGELOG cites only section 10.

summary: The change adds `athena-core::host_rules::check_host_rules`. It makes two plain `gh api` GET calls to `repos/{owner}/{repo}/rules/branches/{branch}`, one for athena/records and one for main. It reports three rules, each as in force, not in force, or unknown: force-push forbidden, deletion forbidden, and up to date before merging required. It changes no host setting and is not wired into any command. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core host_rules` and all 8 tests passed. They cover the in-force fixtures, the empty list, a strict policy that is false or missing, a partial list, a check that only the two exact GET calls are made, 403 and 503 failures, a reply that is not JSON, a reply that is an object instead of a list, one branch failing while the other succeeds, and the plain-text report. The doc comments match the D111 requirement in design §3 (lines 80–84). The module is registered in lib.rs. Every changed file is on the deliverables list. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test runs all passed. I found one minor issue. The module doc says the rules view lists every rule that applies to a branch "whatever its source". From what I know of GitHub's API (I did not check it here), that endpoint returns ruleset rules but not classic branch protection. So a rule Sri sets through classic protection would show as "not in force". The accepted reading chose the rulesets view, so this does not fail a criterion, but the wording overstates what the check sees.
